gaps.statement: Pathways are not consistently compared using durability-adjusted lifecycle accounting.
Reversal and leakage timescales are rarely represented explicitly across geological, biological, and ocean pathways.
Monitoring, reporting, and verification are often treated as reporting rather than as a capacity and cost constraint.
Energy, land, water, mineral supply, transport, and ecological constraints interact at scale.
Global removal objectives can hide local resource and environmental-justice burdens.
Long-term stewardship, liability, and trigger rules after project finance are under-specified.

rejected_overclaims: All captured CO2 is permanently stored.
Biological carbon pools are equivalent to geological reservoirs.
Future CDR can justify delaying gross emissions reductions.
Nominal storage capacity equals deployable, monitored, and socially acceptable capacity.
